body.explanation: We should fear, love, and trust in God above all things.
body.name: The First Commandment
body.text: Thou shalt have no other gods.

verses.question: God Alone as Judge
verses.text: And one of the company said unto him, Master, speak to my brother, that he divide the inheritance with me.

verses.question: God Alone as Judge
verses.text: And he said unto him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?

verses.question: Trusting God Above Created Things
verses.text: Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, ye that are escaped of the nations: they have no knowledge that set up the wood of their graven image, and pray unto a god that cannot save.

verses.question: Trusting God Above Created Things
verses.text: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.

verses.question: Trusting God Above Created Things
verses.text: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

verses.question: Worship God Alone
verses.text: I am the LORD: that is my name: and my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.

verses.question: Worship God Alone
verses.text: Then saith Jesus unto him, Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

verses.question: Worship God Alone
verses.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

verses.question: Worship God Alone
verses.text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

verses.question: Worship God Alone
verses.text: As concerning therefore the eating of those things that are offered in sacrifice unto idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is none other God but one.

verses.question: Fear, Love, and Trust in God
verses.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: a good understanding have all they that do his commandments: his praise endureth for ever.

verses.question: Fear, Love, and Trust in God
verses.text: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.

verses.question: Fear, Love, and Trust in God
verses.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

verses.question: The One True God of All Nations
verses.text: All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee.

verses.question: The One True God of All Nations
verses.text: For in him we live, and move, and have our being; as certain also of your own poets have said, For we are also his offspring.

verses.question: The One True God of All Nations
verses.text: Forasmuch then as we are the offspring of God, we ought not to think that the Godhead is like unto gold, or silver, or stone, graven by art and man’s device.

verses.question: The One True God of All Nations
verses.text: For though there be that are called gods, whether in heaven or in earth, (as there be gods many, and lords many,)

verses.question: The One True God of All Nations
verses.text: But to us there is but one God, the Father, of whom are all things, and we in him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things, and we by him.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: The fear of the LORD is to hate evil: pride, and arrogancy, and the evil way, and the froward mouth, do I hate.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: For the LORD is great, and greatly to be praised: he is to be feared above all gods.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the LORD made the heavens.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: Honour and majesty are before him: strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: Give unto the LORD, O ye kindreds of the people, give unto the LORD glory and strength.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name: bring an offering, and come into his courts.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: O worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness: fear before him, all the earth.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: Say among the heathen that the LORD reigneth: the world also shall be established that it shall not be moved: he shall judge the people righteously.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: Let the heavens rejoice, and let the earth be glad; let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof.

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: Let the field be joyful, and all that is therein: then shall all the trees of the wood rejoice

verses.question: Fearing God Above All
verses.text: Before the Lord: for he cometh, for he cometh to judge the earth: he shall judge the world with righteousness, and the people with his truth.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: Whom have I in heaven but thee? and there is none upon earth that I desire beside thee.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: My flesh and my heart faileth: but God is the strength of my heart, and my portion for ever.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: If ye love me, keep my commandments.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And when he was gone forth into the way, there came one running, and kneeled to him, and asked him, Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? there is none good but one, that is, God.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour thy father and mother.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And he answered and said unto him, Master, all these have I observed from my youth.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: Then Jesus beholding him loved him, and said unto him, One thing thou lackest: go thy way, sell whatsoever thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, take up the cross, and follow me.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And Jesus looked round about, and saith unto his disciples, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And the disciples were astonished at his words. But Jesus answereth again, and saith unto them, Children, how hard is it for them that trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And they were astonished out of measure, saying among themselves, Who then can be saved?

verses.question: Loving God Above All
verses.text: And Jesus looking upon them saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God: for with God all things are possible.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Humble yourselves therefore under the mighty hand of God, that he may exalt you in due time:

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Let your moderation be known unto all men. The Lord is at hand.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Be not wise in thine own eyes: fear the LORD, and depart from evil.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: It shall be health to thy navel, and marrow to thy bones.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Honour the LORD with thy substance, and with the firstfruits of all thine increase:

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: So shall thy barns be filled with plenty, and thy presses shall burst out with new wine.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men’s hands.

verses.question: Trusting God Above All
verses.text: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And the whole earth was of one language, and of one speech.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And it came to pass, as they journeyed from the east, that they found a plain in the land of Shinar; and they dwelt there.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And they said one to another, Go to, let us make brick, and burn them throughly. And they had brick for stone, and slime had they for morter.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And they said, Go to, let us build us a city and a tower, whose top may reach unto heaven; and let us make us a name, lest we be scattered abroad upon the face of the whole earth.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men builded.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And the LORD said, Behold, the people is one, and they have all one language; and this they begin to do: and now nothing will be restrained from them, which they have imagined to do.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Go to, let us go down, and there confound their language, that they may not understand one another’s speech.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: So the LORD scattered them abroad from thence upon the face of all the earth: and they left off to build the city.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Therefore is the name of it called Babel; because the LORD did there confound the language of all the earth: and from thence did the LORD scatter them abroad upon the face of all the earth.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And he spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others:

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And a certain ruler asked him, saying, Good Master, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And Jesus said unto him, Why callest thou me good? none is good, save one, that is, God.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Thou knowest the commandments, Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Honour thy father and thy mother.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And he said, All these have I kept from my youth up.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Now when Jesus heard these things, he said unto him, Yet lackest thou one thing: sell all that thou hast, and distribute unto the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come, follow me.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And when he heard this, he was very sorrowful: for he was very rich.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And when Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, How hardly shall they that have riches enter into the kingdom of God!

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats: but God shall destroy both it and them. Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And God hath both raised up the Lord, and will also raise up us by his own power.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Know ye not that your bodies are the members of Christ? shall I then take the members of Christ, and make them the members of an harlot? God forbid.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: What? know ye not that he which is joined to an harlot is one body? for two, saith he, shall be one flesh.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: But he that is joined unto the Lord is one spirit.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: Flee fornication. Every sin that a man doeth is without the body; but he that committeth fornication sinneth against his own body.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: And he that taketh not his cross, and followeth after me, is not worthy of me.

verses.question: Idols of Pride and Self
verses.text: He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And when the people saw that Moses delayed to come down out of the mount, the people gathered themselves together unto Aaron, and said unto him, Up, make us gods, which shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man that brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we wot not what is become of him.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And Aaron said unto them, Break off the golden earrings, which are in the ears of your wives, of your sons, and of your daughters, and bring them unto me.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And all the people brake off the golden earrings which were in their ears, and brought them unto Aaron.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And he received them at their hand, and fashioned it with a graving tool, after he had made it a molten calf: and they said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it; and Aaron made proclamation, and said, To morrow is a feast to the LORD.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And they rose up early on the morrow, and offered burnt offerings, and brought peace offerings; and the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, Go, get thee down; for thy people, which thou broughtest out of the land of Egypt, have corrupted themselves:

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: They have turned aside quickly out of the way which I commanded them: they have made them a molten calf, and have worshipped it, and have sacrificed thereunto, and said, These be thy gods, O Israel, which have brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And the LORD said unto Moses, I have seen this people, and, behold, it is a stiffnecked people:

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: Now therefore let me alone, that my wrath may wax hot against them, and that I may consume them: and I will make of thee a great nation.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

verses.question: The Idolatry of the Heart
verses.text: For this ye know, that no whoremonger, nor unclean person, nor covetous man, who is an idolater, hath any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and of God.

verses.question: Seeking God First
verses.text: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

verses.question: Seeking God First
verses.text: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:

verses.question: Seeking God First
verses.text: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.

verses.question: Seeking God First
verses.text: He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.

verses.question: No One Is Without Sin
verses.text: For there is not a just man upon earth, that doeth good, and sinneth not.

verses.question: No One Is Without Sin
verses.text: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: And the earth was without form and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: And Jesus, when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: The same was in the beginning with God.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Ghost, be with you all. Amen. The second epistle to the Corinthians was written from Philippi, a city of Macedonia, by Titus and Lucas.

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee:

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee:

verses.question: God the Holy Trinity
verses.text: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: The LORD is good to all: and his tender mercies are over all his works.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: If we believe not, yet he abideth faithful: he cannot deny himself.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: For I am the LORD, I change not; therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. O LORD, thou hast searched me, and known me.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O LORD, thou knowest it altogether.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the LORD. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the LORD.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: He is the Rock, his work is perfect: for all his ways are judgment: a God of truth and without iniquity, just and right is he.

verses.question: The Attributes of God
verses.text: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.

verses.question: The First Commandment
verses.text: And God spake all these words, saying,

verses.question: The First Commandment
verses.text: I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.

verses.question: The First Commandment
verses.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.

verses.question: The First Commandment
verses.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.

verses.question: The First Commandment
verses.text: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth:

verses.question: The First Commandment
verses.text: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me;

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Then answered Jesus and said unto them, Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth: and he will shew him greater works than these, that ye may marvel.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For as the Father raiseth up the dead, and quickeneth them; even so the Son quickeneth whom he will.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son:

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: That all men should honour the Son, even as they honour the Father. He that honoureth not the Son honoureth not the Father which hath sent him.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And ye will not come to me, that ye might have life.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: I receive not honour from men.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only?

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And it was at Jerusalem the feast of the dedication, and it was winter.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And Jesus walked in the temple in Solomon’s porch.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Then came the Jews round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou make us to doubt? If thou be the Christ, tell us plainly.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believed not: the works that I do in my Father’s name, they bear witness of me.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: I and my Father are one.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And it came to pass in those days, that the Philistines gathered their armies together for warfare, to fight with Israel. And Achish said unto David, Know thou assuredly, that thou shalt go out with me to battle, thou and thy men.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And David said to Achish, Surely thou shalt know what thy servant can do. And Achish said to David, Therefore will I make thee keeper of mine head for ever.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Now Samuel was dead, and all Israel had lamented him, and buried him in Ramah, even in his own city. And Saul had put away those that had familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And the Philistines gathered themselves together, and came and pitched in Shunem: and Saul gathered all Israel together, and they pitched in Gilboa.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And when Saul enquired of the LORD, the LORD answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Then said Saul unto his servants, Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her. And his servants said to him, Behold, there is a woman that hath a familiar spirit at En–dor.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And Saul disguised himself, and put on other raiment, and he went, and two men with him, and they came to the woman by night: and he said, I pray thee, divine unto me by the familiar spirit, and bring me him up, whom I shall name unto thee.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And the woman said unto him, Behold, thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And Saul sware to her by the LORD, saying, As the LORD liveth, there shall no punishment happen to thee for this thing.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Then said the woman, Whom shall I bring up unto thee? And he said, Bring me up Samuel.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And when the woman saw Samuel, she cried with a loud voice: and the woman spake to Saul, saying, Why hast thou deceived me? for thou art Saul.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And the king said unto her, Be not afraid: for what sawest thou? And the woman said unto Saul, I saw gods ascending out of the earth.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And he said unto her, What form is he of? And she said, An old man cometh up; and he is covered with a mantle. And Saul perceived that it was Samuel, and he stooped with his face to the ground, and bowed himself.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And Samuel said to Saul, Why hast thou disquieted me, to bring me up? And Saul answered, I am sore distressed; for the Philistines make war against me, and God is departed from me, and answereth me no more, neither by prophets, nor by dreams: therefore I have called thee, that thou mayest make known unto me what I shall do.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Then said Samuel, Wherefore then dost thou ask of me, seeing the LORD is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy?

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And the LORD hath done to him, as he spake by me: for the LORD hath rent the kingdom out of thine hand, and given it to thy neighbour, even to David:

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Because thou obeyedst not the voice of the LORD, nor executedst his fierce wrath upon Amalek, therefore hath the LORD done this thing unto thee this day.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Moreover the LORD will also deliver Israel with thee into the hand of the Philistines: and to morrow shalt thou and thy sons be with me: the LORD also shall deliver the host of Israel into the hand of the Philistines.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Then Saul fell straightway all along on the earth, and was sore afraid, because of the words of Samuel: and there was no strength in him; for he had eaten no bread all the day, nor all the night.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And the woman came unto Saul, and saw that he was sore troubled, and said unto him, Behold, thine handmaid hath obeyed thy voice, and I have put my life in my hand, and have hearkened unto thy words which thou spakest unto me.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: Now therefore, I pray thee, hearken thou also unto the voice of thine handmaid, and let me set a morsel of bread before thee; and eat, that thou mayest have strength, when thou goest on thy way.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: But he refused, and said, I will not eat. But his servants, together with the woman, compelled him; and he hearkened unto their voice. So he arose from the earth, and sat upon the bed.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And the woman had a fat calf in the house; and she hasted, and killed it, and took flour, and kneaded it, and did bake unleavened bread thereof:

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: And she brought it before Saul, and before his servants; and they did eat. Then they rose up, and went away that night.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt, they have done abominable works, there is none that doeth good.

verses.question: Unbelief and False Worship
verses.text: To the chief Musician upon Mahalath, Maschil, A Psalm of David. The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God. Corrupt are they, and have done abominable iniquity: there is none that doeth good.

verses.question: The Two Ways
verses.text: Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.

verses.question: The Two Ways
verses.text: But his delight is in the law of the LORD; and in his law doth he meditate day and night.

verses.question: The Two Ways
verses.text: And he shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season; his leaf also shall not wither; and whatsoever he doeth shall prosper.

verses.question: The Two Ways
verses.text: The ungodly are not so: but are like the chaff which the wind driveth away.

verses.question: The Two Ways
verses.text: Therefore the ungodly shall not stand in the judgment, nor sinners in the congregation of the righteous.

verses.question: The Two Ways
verses.text: For the Lord knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.

verses.question: The Deuteronomy 5 Parallel
verses.text: Thou shalt have none other gods before me.
In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
And the earth was without form and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
And God said, Let there be light: and there was light.
And God saw the light, that it was good: and God divided the light from the darkness.
And God called the light Day, and the darkness he called Night. And the evening and the morning were the first day.
And God said, Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide the waters from the waters.
And God made the firmament, and divided the waters which were under the firmament from the waters which were above the firmament: and it was so.
And God called the firmament Heaven. And the evening and the morning were the second day.
And God said, Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear: and it was so.
And God called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and God saw that it was good.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.
And the earth brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after his kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after his kind: and God saw that it was good.
And the evening and the morning were the third day.
And God said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:
And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth: and it was so.
And God made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.
And God set them in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth,
And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and God saw that it was good.
And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.
And God said, Let the waters bring forth abundantly the moving creature that hath life, and fowl that may fly above the earth in the open firmament of heaven.
And God created great whales, and every living creature that moveth, which the waters brought forth abundantly, after their kind, and every winged fowl after his kind: and God saw that it was good.
And God blessed them, saying, Be fruitful, and multiply, and fill the waters in the seas, and let fowl multiply in the earth.
And the evening and the morning were the fifth day.
And God said, Let the earth bring forth the living creature after his kind, cattle, and creeping thing, and beast of the earth after his kind: and it was so.
And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.

And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.

And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.

And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.
And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.
And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.

body.description: A stronghold of the Canaanites in the mountains north of Lake Merom ([Josh. 11:1-5](/josh#Josh.11.1)). Jabin the king with his allied tribes here encountered Joshua in a great battle. Joshua gained a signal victory, which virtually completed his conquest of Canaan (11:10-13). This city was, however, afterwards rebuilt by the Canaanites, and was ruled by a king with the same hereditary name of Jabin. His army, under a noted leader of the name of Sisera, swept down upon the south, aiming at the complete subjugation of the country. This powerful army was met by the Israelites under Barak, who went forth by the advice of the prophetess Deborah. The result was one of the most remarkable victories for Israel recorded in the Old Testament ([Josh. 19:36](/josh#Josh.19.36); [Judg. 4:2](/judg#Judg.4.2); [1 Sam. 12:9](/1sam#1Sam.12.9)). The city of Hazor was taken and occupied by the Israelites. It was fortified by Solomon to defend the entrance into the kingdom from Syria and Assyria. When Tiglath-pileser, the Assyrian king, invaded the land, this was one of the first cities he captured, carrying its inhabitants captive into Assyria ([2 Kings 15:29](/2kgs#2Kgs.15.29)). It has been identified with Khurbet Harrah, 2 1/2 miles south-east of Kedesh.

fall.event: Alexander dies; his empire divides among four successor kingdoms
fall.ref_note: Daniel 8:8,22 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the he-goat's great horn 'broken,' replaced by 'four notable ones toward the four winds of heaven' (v.8), self-interpreted a few verses later as 'four kingdoms shall stand up out of the nation' (v.22); traditionally dated to Alexander's 323 BC death -- see this era's own rise-transition for the same vision's earlier verses

transition.event: Alexander the Great conquers the Achaemenid Persian Empire
transition.ref_note: Daniel 8:5,20-21 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the he-goat 'from the west' (v.5), self-interpreted in the text as Grecia overthrowing Media-Persia (vv.20-21); traditionally dated 334-330 BC -- see egypt.toml's own mirrored transition for the same conquest's reach into Egypt

fall.event: The Medes and Neo-Babylonians destroy Nineveh
fall.ref_note: Nahum 3:18-19 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the whole book of Nahum is a prophecy of Nineveh's own destruction, traditionally dated 612 BC; these closing verses address the king of Assyria's own ruin directly

transition.event: The Neo-Assyrian resurgence begins under Adad-nirari II
transition.ref_note: general Assyriological knowledge (the 10th-9th century BC resurgence that becomes the Neo-Assyrian Empire); no specific source consulted this session; not scripture-narrated at this specific boundary -- the KJV text's own Assyria narrative picks up later, once the empire already presses on Israel (e.g. 2 Kings 15:19)

fall.event: Babylon falls; Belshazzar is slain in the night
fall.ref_note: Daniel 5:30-31 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- 'In that night was Belshazzar the king of the Chaldeans slain... And Darius the Median took the kingdom,' traditionally dated 539 BC -- see persia.toml's own mirrored rise-transition

transition.event: Nabopolassar revolts against Assyria, founding the Neo-Babylonian dynasty
transition.ref_note: general historical knowledge (Nabopolassar's own 626 BC revolt, allied with the Medes, that leads to Nineveh's fall -- see assyria.toml's own fall); no specific source consulted this session; Nabopolassar himself is not named in the KJV text

transition.event: The Hyksos are expelled; the New Kingdom and the Egyptian Empire begin
transition.ref_note: general Egyptological knowledge (Ahmose I's expulsion of the Hyksos, founding the 18th Dynasty); no specific source consulted this session; not otherwise scripture-narrated at this specific boundary

transition.event: The New Kingdom collapses; Egypt contracts back to the Nile valley
transition.ref_note: general Egyptological knowledge (the Late Bronze Age Collapse; Ramesses XI's own weak final reign ending the Empire); no specific source consulted this session; not otherwise scripture-narrated

fall.event: Rome annexes Egypt after Actium; Cleopatra dies
fall.ref_note: general Roman/Ptolemaic history (Battle of Actium and its aftermath, 31-30 BC); no specific source consulted this session; not scripture-narrated -- this era predates the Gospel narrative entirely

transition.event: Alexander the Great conquers Egypt, ending Persian rule
transition.ref_note: Daniel 8:20-21 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Daniel's own vision, self-interpreted in the text as Media-Persia (the ram) overthrown by Grecia (the goat); Egypt was a Persian satrapy at the time (persia.toml), so this same prophecy applies here as it does to Persia's own fall/alexander-empire.toml's own rise

transition.event: David is anointed king over all Israel
transition.ref_note: 2 Samuel 5:1,3 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- all the tribes come to David at Hebron and anoint him king over Israel, the moment this era's own name ("United Monarchy") describes

fall.ref_note: 2 Kings 17:6,23 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- fall of Samaria and the deportation to Assyria, traditionally dated 722 BC

transition.event: The kingdom divides; Jeroboam is made king over Israel
transition.ref_note: 1 Kings 12:16,20 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Israel rejects Rehoboam ('to your tents, O Israel') and makes Jeroboam king; Judah alone follows the house of David (see judah.toml's own mirrored transition)

transition.event: The kingdom divides; Judah alone follows the house of David
transition.ref_note: 1 Kings 12:16,19 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Israel rejects Rehoboam and rebels 'against the house of David unto this day'; Judah (this polity) is what remains loyal to it -- see israel.toml's own mirrored transition

transition.event: Cyrus decrees the return from exile and the rebuilding of the temple
transition.ref_note: Ezra 1:1-3 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Cyrus's own proclamation, traditionally dated 538 BC; the destruction that precedes this gap is Judah's OWN previous era's own end (2 Kings 25, not separately cited here since it falls chronologically inside the gap between these two eras, not at either one's own boundary)

transition.event: The Maccabean Revolt overthrows Seleucid rule in Judea
transition.ref_note: the revolt itself (167-160 BC) is narrated in 1 Maccabees, outside the KJV's 66-book canon -- not otherwise cited here; Daniel 11:31 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) is the prophecy traditionally read as depicting Antiochus IV's own desecration of the temple, the revolt's proximate trigger -- a prophetic application, not a narrative citation, disclosed as such

fall.event: Herod the Great dies; his kingdom is partitioned among his sons
fall.ref_note: Matthew 2:19 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- 'when Herod was dead'; the partition itself (Matthew 2:22's own Archelaus reigning 'in the room of his father Herod') is general history/Josephus for the specific three-way split, traditionally dated 4 BC

transition.event: Rome installs Herod the Great as king of Judea
transition.ref_note: Josephus (Antiquities 14/Jewish War 1), general history -- not narrated in the KJV text, which first names Herod near his own death (Matthew 2); no verse cited rather than an invented one

transition.event: Cyrus conquers Babylon, founding the Achaemenid Persian Empire
transition.ref_note: Isaiah 44:28, 45:1 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- Isaiah names Cyrus by name as the Lord's own 'anointed,' generations before his reign; the conquest itself is narrated in Daniel 5 (see babylon.toml's own mirrored fall-transition), traditionally dated 539 BC

fall.event: Nebuchadnezzar besieges Tyre; Neo-Babylonian then Persian rule absorbs the coast
fall.ref_note: Ezekiel 26:3-4,7 (KJV, verified against the compiled text) -- the Lord's own oracle against Tyre, naming 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' directly (v.7); the historical thirteen-year siege and the coast's later absorption into Persian control are general history beyond what these verses themselves narrate

transition.event: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium; the Senate names him Augustus
transition.ref_note: Actium (31 BC) and the Senate's own grant of the Augustus title (27 BC) are general Roman history -- not narrated or prophesied anywhere in the KJV text at this specific boundary; no verse cited rather than one (Luke 2:1's own later, unrelated census reference) that would risk reading as though it narrated this event under a THE SCRIPTURES heading

fall.event: Pompey annexes Syria as a Roman province, ending Seleucid rule
fall.ref_note: general Roman/Hellenistic historical knowledge (Pompey's own 64/63 BC settlement of the East); no specific source consulted this session; 1 Maccabees, the fullest narrative source for the Seleucid decline, is outside the KJV's 66-book canon

transition.event: Parthian and Armenian conquests reduce the Seleucid realm to a rump state
transition.ref_note: general Hellenistic-era historical knowledge (Parthia's own mid-2nd-century BC eastward conquests under Mithridates I; Tigranes of Armenia's own later inroads); no specific source consulted this session; not scripture-narrated

sources.title: The King James Version
sources.what_it_is: The King James Version of the Holy Bible -- the canonical English text this app reads, cites, and builds every other layer around.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into verses-kjv.json and canon.json: the book/chapter/verse structure and the verse text itself, obtained via the scrollmapper/bible_databases project. Every other translation this app carries rides alongside this text; none ever replaces it.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Geocoding
sources.what_it_is: Place-coordinate data for the locations named throughout Scripture, from OpenBible.info's Bible-Geocoding-Data project.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into places.json, giving mapped places their coordinates on the World page.

sources.title: OpenBible.info Cross-References
sources.what_it_is: A cross-reference dataset connecting related passages across the whole Bible.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into cross-refs.json, powering the reader's own cross-reference lookups.

sources.title: KJV Red-Letter Markup
sources.what_it_is: A words-of-Christ annotation layer tracing back to Louis Klopsch's 1901 red-letter edition, obtained through eBible.org's own public-domain KJV OSIS distribution (via the seven1m/open-bibles collection).
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into SpokenBy/SpokenAt graph edges and data/compiled/red-letter-spans.json, which color Christ's own words wherever verse text renders in the reader. An annotation over our own KJV text, never a change to it.

sources.title: brain-fuel/bible Parallel Editions
sources.what_it_is: Six further public-domain Bible editions: the Clementine Vulgate, the Westminster Leningrad Codex, the Douay-Rheims (Challoner), Biblia 1776, Karl XII:s Bibel (1703), and the Greek Textus Receptus.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled as additional translation layers in the graph, alongside -- never replacing -- this app's own canonical KJV text.

sources.title: STEPBible TAGNT / TAHOT / TBESG (Tyndale House Cambridge)
sources.what_it_is: STEPBible's Translators Amalgamated Greek NT (TAGNT), Translators Amalgamated Hebrew OT (TAHOT), and Translators Brief Exhaustive Strong's Greek (TBESG): per-word lemma, morphology, Strong's numbers and English glosses for the Greek NT and Hebrew OT, produced by STEPBible and Tyndale House Cambridge.
sources.what_we_built: Every original-language word in the reader is aligned to its Strong's lexicon entry (the graph's Occurs rows: a verse's `words`, an entry's `occurs-in` concordance, in canonical order), and each Greek entry carries TBESG's brief English gloss. Alignment is by original-language word only -- no English word is tagged. Credit STEPBible and link to https://github.com/STEPBible.

sources.title: MACULA Greek and Hebrew Linguistic Datasets (Clear Bible Inc.)
sources.what_it_is: Clear Bible's MACULA datasets: Louw-Nida section references for the Greek NT and SDBH lexical-domain codes for the Hebrew OT (semantic domains per word).
sources.what_we_built: Each lexicon entry carries its sorted semantic-domain codes (the lexicon section's domain table), written so a later thesaurus-by-domain query can answer from them; no endpoint reads them yet.

sources.title: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance dictionaries (James Strong, 1890)
sources.what_it_is: James Strong's 1890 Greek and Hebrew dictionaries, numbered G1-G5624 and H1-H8674 (XML encoding by Ulrik Petersen / openscriptures), the numbering every other lexical source here keys on.
sources.what_we_built: The 13,548 lexicon entries themselves: Strong's number, lemma, transliteration, part of speech, the 1890 definition text as the first English gloss, and the root-word link. Ingested as upstream publishes it (upstream normalises the tetragrammaton to 'Yahweh' in Strong's own PD gloss text; the KJV column is never edited).

sources.title: Theographic Bible Metadata
sources.what_it_is: A rich, hand-built dataset of biblical people, places, and events with dates, by Robert Rouse.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into events.json and much of places.json -- the great majority of this app's dated, narrative content rests on this dataset.

sources.title: Robertson's Harmony of the Gospels
sources.what_it_is: A.T. Robertson's A Harmony of the Gospels for Students of the Life of Christ (1922), which orders and groups the four Gospels' own parallel accounts.
sources.what_we_built: Robertson's own section numbers, titles, and groupings guided event-witnesses.toml's parallel-witness groupings and Passion Week's own chronological order. Every displayed event title and verse citation is this project's own, provenance-tagged (robertson_section) back to the section that grounded it.

sources.title: Crockett's Harmony of Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles
sources.what_it_is: William Day Crockett's A Harmony of the Books of Samuel, Kings and Chronicles (1897).
sources.what_we_built: Crockett's own section groupings guided the parallel-witness rows connecting Samuel, Kings, and Chronicles (and their related passages). Every displayed event title and verse citation is this project's own.

sources.title: Ussher's Annals of the World
sources.what_it_is: James Ussher's The Annals of the World (1658), a chronology of biblical and ancient history.
sources.what_we_built: Two of its own paragraph-numbered entries grounded two chronology-anchors.toml year values: Ezra's return, and the completion of Nehemiah's wall.

sources.license: Public domain (carried in the vendored Theographic bundle, itself CC BY-SA 4.0)
sources.title: Easton's Bible Dictionary
sources.what_it_is: M. G. Easton's Bible Dictionary (1897), describing who and what the people and places of Scripture are.
sources.what_we_built: Its own entries fill the description shown on Place, Person, and PeopleGroup cards throughout the app, delivered via the already-vendored Theographic bundle.

sources.title: Kretzmann's Popular Commentary of the Bible
sources.what_it_is: Paul E. Kretzmann's Popular Commentary of the Bible (Concordia Publishing House, 1921-1924) -- verse-by-verse commentary across the whole Bible.
sources.what_we_built: Kretzmann's own commentary prose (never the KJV text his own commentary quotes) is compiled into verse-anchored commentary entries throughout the reader. A tentative date-mining pass over that same prose also surfaces the B.C./A.D. years Kretzmann mentions (data/exports/kretzmann-chronology.json, honestly marked tentative-extraction -- a future curatorial pass, not this app's chronology of record, adjudicates real placements from it).

sources.title: Luther's Small Catechism
sources.what_it_is: Martin Luther's Small Catechism -- the Ten Commandments, the Creed, the Lord's Prayer, and the Sacraments -- in the 1921 Bente-Dau English translation (Triglot Concordia / Concordia Triglotta).
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into catechism.json, in Luther's own words, with verse links drawn from Luther's own citations and from the mapping below.

sources.title: The Book of Concord
sources.what_it_is: The Lutheran church's confessional writings, in the same 1921 Bente-Dau translation as the Small Catechism above.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into the graph as a second full reading corpus alongside Scripture, paragraph by paragraph.

sources.license: No license file -- used by the project owner's own explicit direction
sources.title: Catechism Verse Mapping
sources.what_it_is: A mapping of Scripture references to Small Catechism questions, from the brain-fuel/catechism project, used here by the project owner's own direction.
sources.what_we_built: Compiled into catechism.json's own per-question verse links, connecting the Catechism to Scripture throughout the reader.

sources.title: Esri World Shaded Relief
sources.what_it_is: The label-free, light-terrain basemap tiles behind the World page's map -- relief, coastlines, and water tone, with every label of our own drawn on top.
sources.what_we_built: Fetched live by the browser from Esri's own servers at runtime -- never stored or redistributed by this app -- attributed on the map itself and here, verbatim: "Copyright:(c) 2014 Esri".

sources.title: Carto Basemap Tiles
sources.what_it_is: A fallback set of basemap tiles, used only if the Esri tile service is unreachable.
sources.what_we_built: Fetched live by the browser at runtime, the same as Esri above -- never stored or redistributed by this app.

sources.title: Leaflet
sources.what_it_is: The open-source JavaScript map library that renders the World page.
sources.what_we_built: Vendored and committed at client/wwwroot/vendor/leaflet/ (v1.9.4, upstream copyright banner retained), so a fresh clone runs without any fetch step.

sources.title: Our Own Curated Work
sources.what_it_is: Everything this project authored directly: the historical polity borders, the coastline land mask, biblical landmarks, narrative threads, eras, and the titles, sectioning, and aliases that connect it all together.
sources.what_we_built: Hand-authored under data/curated/ and compiled into narratives.json, eras.json, books-meta.json, landmarks.json, polities.json, and land-mask.json. Every displayed event title is this project's own phrasing, provenance-tagged (robertson_section, acts_section, kjv_superscription, theographic, atlas_section) back to whichever source above grounded it, so the mapping stays auditable.

catechism.name: What Does God Say of All These Commandments?
catechism.question: Redemption in Christ

cross_refs.preview: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.
He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?
That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
And this is the will of him that sent me, that every one which seeth the Son, and believeth on him, may have everlasting life: and I will raise him up at the last day.
He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him.
We love him, because he first loved us.
And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief.
For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.
The next day John seeth Jesus coming unto him, and saith, Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.
Now our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, which hath loved us, and hath given us everlasting consolation and good hope through grace,
To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.
But God, who is rich in mercy, for his great love wherewith he loved us,
But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
And from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, and the first begotten of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth. Unto him that loved us, and washed us from our sins in his own blood,
And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.
And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
But after that the kindness and love of God our Saviour toward man appeared,
No man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son, which is in the bosom of the Father, he hath declared him.
Having yet therefore one son, his wellbeloved, he sent him also last unto them, saying, They will reverence my son.
Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.

events.label: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night

body.text: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
